rounds.text: Indo Euro Indchem Ltd is significantly under-appreciated by the market, trading at an attractive price-to-book ratio of 0.69x against a sector benchmark of 3.77x [E7]. The company presents a compelling margin of safety of 37.3%, with a discounted cash flow model placing intrinsic value at Rs 14 per share compared to a market price of Rs 9 [E44, E45]. Furthermore, a reverse DCF indicates that the current price only implies a 12.1% earnings growth rate, which sits comfortably below the 18.0% base case assumption [E46]. Long-term performance underscores robust underlying fundamentals, demonstrated by a 10-year compounded profit growth of 24% and a 5-year compounded profit growth of 36%, heavily outpacing the multi-year share price declines [E18, E19, E23, E24, E25]. Balance sheet health is exceptional with a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.00x and completely flat borrowings of Rs 0.00 Cr, while recent operational efficiency has improved dramatically as debtor days compressed from 245 to 81.1 days [E38, E39, E61]. Conceded: [E10], [E21], [E63].

The bull leans heavily on a low price-to-book ratio of 0.69x, but this multiple must be weighed against chronically depressed returns on capital, including a meager 3.8% ROCE and a 2.8% ROE [E10, E13]. Conceded: [E7], [E18], [E19], [E38], [E39], [E61]. While a discounted cash flow model suggests intrinsic value at Rs 14, recent performance tells a story of severe deterioration with trailing twelve-month profit plunging 51% alongside a 1% drop in sales [E21, E44]. The claim of exceptional long-term profit growth fails to justify the current stock price given that multi-year share price growth has been negative, showing a 33% decline over 3 years and a 32% drop over 1 year [E24, E25]. Furthermore, the technical and sentiment profile remains toxic, evidenced by a relative-strength rating of zero, a price sitting below both the 50-day and 200-day moving averages, and a massive historical peak-to-trough drawdown of 100% [E49, E50, E52].
